papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.venue: NIPS 2017 / Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30
papers.version: conference-hosted full PDF downloaded 2026-10-06; not latest arXiv
papers.completion_scope: all physical pages in selected frozen PDF, including references; external supplements are outside this version and not claimed read
papers.prior_read: selective architecture read in T25; this T24 read expands coverage; not newly discovered Agent research
papers.selection_reason: Same mathematical operator as attention working paper; teaches overview/operator separation and cost-vs-quality argument.
papers.quality_reason: Useful because definitions, analytical table and controlled ablations form a traceable argument; reputation alone is not the criterion.
limitations: Official proceedings identity re-opened 2026-10-06 (web ref turn107view0). Its HTML abstract has 27.5/41.1 rather than frozen PDF 28.4/41.0; do not mix versions.
All 11 selected pages read; external appendix mentioned on p7 not present and not read.
No training reproduction; exemplar metrics are source facts only.

organization.observation: Problem and background lead to architecture, then analytical justification, reproducible training and outcome/ablation results. The method is defined before the cost argument, so readers can map symbols to operations.
organization.transfer: For attention study: define exact operator, isolate proposed approximation, derive what changes, then measure error/cost. For runtime study: failure observation→state semantics→scheduler policy→tests.
organization.counterexample_or_limit: This neural architecture paper is not a systems template: large training section and leaderboard narrative do not transfer to a small local runtime study.

claim_evidence.location: p6 Table1; p8 Table2; p9 Table3
claim_evidence.observation: Analytical parallelism, translation result, and component sensitivity use different evidence objects. n<d qualifies the cost comparison; equal-compute heads ablation narrows a confound.
claim_evidence.transfer: Maintain separate claim IDs for exact algebra, approximation error, measured runtime and downstream quality, each with its own test.
claim_evidence.counterexample_or_limit: Original estimated FLOPs are not same-hardware benchmark evidence; no own-paper speedup follows from these tables.

figures.location: p3 Fig1; p4 Fig2; pp6,8,9 Tables1–3
figures.observation: System overview and operator detail are separate; tables carry all comparative numerical evidence. Captions define scope and units rather than relying solely on prose.
figures.transfer: Use one overview plus one changed-operator panel only if both answer distinct questions; include input sizes, precision and units in own performance tables.
figures.counterexample_or_limit: Attention heatmap appendix is absent in this version; no heatmap visual-design claim is supported.

rhetoric.observation: Definitions precede use; suspicion/hypothesis language marks unproven mechanism; EN-FR result is explicitly single-model. Conclusion is stronger and less qualified than some detailed comparisons.
rhetoric.transfer: Use demonstrates for measured invariant, suggests for mechanism interpretation, and untested for extrapolation; avoid blanket faster or exact language.
rhetoric.counterexample_or_limit: Do not borrow first-model or state-of-art rhetoric for an exact-vs-approximation working study; novelty must be independently established.

content.observation: Q/K/V sources, mask value, dimensions, training schedule and evaluation decoding are disclosed near relevant mechanism. Label smoothing improves BLEU while worsening perplexity: different metrics can disagree.
content.transfer: Place approximation constraints and metric tradeoffs in method/results, not a distant limitations checklist; runtime waiting semantics need analogous explicit definitions.
content.counterexample_or_limit: The PDF lacks modern variance reporting for most translation comparisons and lacks the promised appendix; these are counterexamples, not conventions to reproduce.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.version: CVF accepted conference version (open-access watermark); full PDF downloaded 2026-10-06
papers.completion_scope: all physical pages in selected frozen PDF, including references; external supplements are outside this version and not claimed read
papers.prior_read: selective architecture read in T25; this T24 read expands coverage; not newly discovered Agent research
papers.selection_reason: Provides failure-driven mechanistic narrative directly adaptable to runtime waiting and fairness tests; also illustrates controlled architecture changes.
papers.quality_reason: Quality derives from matched plain/residual controls, train/test distinction, ablations and admitted1202 negative boundary, not merely CVPR status.
limitations: CVF full PDF watermark and printed770–778 support publication; existing sources.json retained. Official HTML re-open returned403 (turn107view1), not silently treated as fresh success.
All9 selected pages read; external appendix not included or read.
No ResNet training or detection reproduction.

organization.observation: Observable degradation opens the argument, a small residual block supplies the intervention, related work/mathematics precede controlled experiments. Full architecture and settings bridge theory to evidence.
organization.transfer: Runtime paper should begin with one concrete waiting/retry failure, then state model and invariants, then policy and comparative tests; image study can begin with geometry failure.
organization.counterexample_or_limit: No mandatory conclusion exists here; forcing every paper into fixed sections misses the compact empirical narrative.

claim_evidence.location: p1 Fig1; p5 Fig4/Table2; p8 Fig6
claim_evidence.observation: Higher training error rules out the simple overfitting story for plain networks; matched depth/width/parameters test shortcuts.1202 case later separates optimization success from generalization.
claim_evidence.transfer: Use competing explanations: normal wait vs failure, fairness vs throughput, exact output equivalence vs approximate quality; pair each with discriminating evidence.
claim_evidence.counterexample_or_limit: Residual response magnitude inFig7 supports but does not prove the proposed optimization explanation; avoid causal certainty from proxy curves.

figures.observation: Motivation curve, minimal mechanism, full topology, controlled curves and boundary case each have different jobs. Shared axes and style encode comparable conditions.
figures.transfer: Create only figures that answer distinct scientific questions; runtime retry/fairness curves require event count or time units and identical workload.
figures.counterexample_or_limit: Many traces have no variance bands and tiny fonts; these are not desirable export choices for new work.

rhetoric.observation: Hypotheses, arguments and observations are differentiated; the CIFAR section declares its narrower purpose. The one-layer non-result and1202 failure remain visible.
rhetoric.transfer: State what the study isolates and does not measure; phrase synthetic verification as local behavioral evidence, not deployed system reliability.
rhetoric.counterexample_or_limit: Universal generalization rhetoric in intro and solely-attributable detection phrasing exceed what should be copied into a small working paper.

content.location: p4 §3.4; p6 projection/bottleneck; p7 warmup; p8 over1000
content.observation: Implementation details are selected for fair comparison. Bottleneck is a practical compute tradeoff; exceptional warmup and negative depth result are disclosed near outcomes.
content.transfer: Preserve parameter budget, seed/schedule, timeout assumptions, precision and shape settings near relevant experiment; discuss cost of policy changes.
content.counterexample_or_limit: No external appendix was read; detection implementation details referenced there cannot be claimed available from these nine pages.

papers.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.version: arXiv:1505.04597v1 (18 May 2015), author-linked preprint; not Springer typeset proceedings
papers.completion_scope: all physical pages in selected frozen PDF, including references; external supplements are outside this version and not claimed read
papers.prior_read: selective architecture read in T25; this T24 read expands coverage; not newly discovered Agent research
papers.selection_reason: Closest mechanism and geometry match to valid-convolution image-network working paper; also a useful counterexample on component attribution.
papers.quality_reason: Quality comes from explicit geometry, practical border handling and metric transparency; weaker isolated-component evidence is recorded rather than hidden.
limitations: Author-linked arXiv1505.04597v1,18May2015; not Springer typeset proceedings. Official author page turn107view2 and publisher turn110view0 confirm MICCAI2015,9351,234–241 and DOI.
All8 physical pages read; external supplementary segmentation material not read and not counted.
No network training, challenge submission or speed reproduction.

organization.observation: Long introduction embeds related work, two mechanism figures and task constraints before compact architecture/training sections. Results occupy fewer pages than mechanism explanation.
organization.transfer: Valid-convolution paper can let geometry motivate the question before implementation; integrate only related work needed to understand crop/tiling choices.
organization.counterexample_or_limit: Do not copy four-page introduction into a tiny study: use figure+short derivation once and reserve space for discriminating tests.

claim_evidence.location: p3 tiling argument; p4 §2; pp6–7 Tables1–2
claim_evidence.observation: Architecture explains where output support comes from; challenge tables establish task outcomes. Scarce-data success combines network, augmentation and weighted loss.
claim_evidence.transfer: Separate deductive shape/crop assertions from measured seam consistency, accuracy and runtime; own tests need matched padding/tiling configurations.
claim_evidence.counterexample_or_limit: Challenge rankings do not establish a causal benefit of valid convolution alone; no component ablation supports that inference.

figures.location: pp2–3 Figs1–2; p5 Fig3; p7 Fig4
figures.observation: Architecture, operational tiling, training target/weight and prediction example serve four distinct stages. Legends make color semantics explicit; natural images ground the task.
figures.transfer: Adopt input/output support diagram and difference-image evaluation as distinct panels; label synthetic examples and mathematical deductions.
figures.counterexample_or_limit: Original figure assets cannot be copied; observational segmentation images cannot stand in for an unrun image-network study.

rhetoric.location: p2 FCN discussion; p3 design motivations; p6 augmentation; p8 conclusion
rhetoric.observation: Prior FCN work is credited before modifications. Causal connectors explain why cropping and mirroring are needed. Elastic deformation is described as seeming key; final broad applicability is asserted optimistically.
rhetoric.transfer: Use concrete subjects and because clauses linking constraint to choice; preserve uncertainty around unablated components.
rhetoric.counterexample_or_limit: Reject obviously/more elegant value judgments and confidence about many more tasks as generic working-paper prose.

content.location: p4 §§2–3; p5 Eqs1–2; p6 evaluation; p7 data counts
content.observation: Practical shape divisibility, tile/batch tradeoff, loss weights and augmentation parameters are adjacent to mechanism; dataset/metric definitions precede rankings.
content.transfer: Own image study must specify valid/padded operator, pooling arithmetic, border policy, input/output dimensions and independent test source before results.
content.counterexample_or_limit: Eq1 positive log-probability expression cannot be transplanted as a minimization loss without resolving sign convention; lack of isolated ablations is a scientific gap, not a writing convention.

cross_paper_observations.observation: Different orders work because each follows a concrete reader question: operator then cost, failure then intervention, or task constraint then geometry.
cross_paper_observations.decision: Adapt each target around its scientific question; reject a universal section-count template.

cross_paper_observations.decision: Use direct measured verbs for own results, conditional language for mechanisms and explicit untested scope.
